title: When the Diagnosis Requires the Harm: Four in Five Trials That Aim to Prevent the Onset of Depression Admit People Who Have Already Had It
content: Background Prevention trials promise to prevent an event, such as a first depressive or psychotic episode or first drug use, but many count a diagnosis that requires it, and many enrol people who have already had it. Methods Formal analysis; a reanalysis of nested outcomes in two randomized zoster-vaccine programmes; and registry audits of ClinicalTrials.gov depression-prevention and clinical high-risk psychosis trials and their published reports. Results Diagnostic risk equals gate-event risk times the probability of completing the remaining criteria, so fewer diagnoses cannot, at any sample size, show that the event was prevented; in participants who have already had the event, gate risk is 1 in both arms and any effect is on recurrence. In one randomized zoster-vaccine stratum the nested endpoint fell by 67% and the event it requires by 37%, while in two other populations the two estimates nearly coincided; the endpoint alone cannot show which applies. Of 38 trials framed as preventing depression onset or incidence, 31 admitted people who had already had a depressive episode (82%, 95% confidence interval 67–91; 74% under the protocol-named categories only), and 68 of the 72 onset-framed or generically framed trials that admitted them registered a single estimate for first and recurrent episodes; in seven reports giving the figure, the share who had already had one ranged from 1% to 80% (median 33.5%). Of 20 trials in people at clinical high risk for psychosis, 19 counted only psychotic-intensity episodes that outlasted a duration threshold, so fewer transitions cannot be told from shorter episodes. A meta-analysis of depression onset pooled a trial in which 80% had already had an episode, recording 55%. Conclusions A four-question gate audit, three of whose questions are answered from the protocol and baseline data before any outcome is observed, detects the mismatch and states what each trial can claim.
